cards.text: It's the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat's reign over Judah. Jehoram son of Ahab becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria twelve years. He does evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as his father and mother had done.

cards.question: Better than his parents. That's a cookie bragging it's only burnt on ONE side. Jehoram removes the sacred pillar of ___ that his father had made.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, the first king of Israel after the kingdom split (1 Kings 12:20), had caused Israel to commit sins. True or false: Jehoram turns away from those sins.

cards.text: Meet Mesha king of Moab, a sheep breeder who would pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams. I complain about my electric bill, and this man is mailing out a HUNDRED THOUSAND LAMBS.

cards.question: Then Ahab dies. What does Mesha king of Moab do after that?

answers.text: Rebels against the king of Israel
Doubles what he pays to Israel
Asks Israel for a new treaty

cards.text: So King Jehoram sets out from Samaria and mobilizes all Israel. He sends a message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?”

cards.question: True or false: Jehoshaphat king of Judah agrees to go fight Moab with Jehoram.
Jehoshaphat says, “I am as you are, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.” THAT is a friend. Then he asks which way they should go up. What does Jehoram answer?

answers.text: By way of the Desert of Edom
By way of the Wilderness of Zin
By way of the Valley of Jezreel

cards.text: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah and the king of Edom set out, and they travel a roundabout route for seven days. Seven days the LONG way around, friend. My GPS has done me like that.

cards.question: Seven days in, and the army and the animals have no ___.
Three kings, a whole army and nothing to drink. What does the king of Israel say the LORD has done?

answers.text: Summoned three kings to hand them to Moab
Promised to send them rain very soon
Told them to turn around and go home

cards.text: Not “let's pray,” not “let's look around,” just straight to ALAS. But Jehoshaphat has another idea.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat asks if there's a ___ of the LORD there, so they can ___ of the LORD through him.

cards.text: A servant of the king of Israel says Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He “used to pour water on the hands of Elijah,” the prophet the LORD took up to heaven (2 Kings 2:11).

cards.question: No water in camp, and Elisha's résumé says he POURS WATER. True or false: Jehoshaphat says the word of the LORD is with Elisha.

cards.text: So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom go down to him. That's three crowns walking down to see ONE prophet.

cards.question: Three kings come down to Elisha. What does Elisha say to the king of Israel?

answers.text: Go to the prophets of your parents
Welcome and tell me what you need
Come back and see me tomorrow

cards.text: “No,” replies the king of Israel, “for it is the LORD who has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab.” That line again. The man has ONE speech and he is STICKING to it.

cards.question: Elisha says, as surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, he wouldn't even look at the king of Israel except for one thing. What is it?

answers.text: His regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah
The thirsty soldiers and their animals
Jehoram removing the pillar of Baal

cards.text: Elisha is only talking because Jehoshaphat king of Judah is standing there. Then he says, “But now, bring me a harpist.” Three kings, a thirsty army, a desert road, and the man calls for MUSIC.

cards.question: While the harpist plays, what comes upon Elisha?

cards.text: Then Elisha says, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’” Thirsty army, and the plan is... DIGGING?

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says they will see wind and rain before the valley fills with water.
Elisha says this is a ___ matter in the sight of the LORD, and He will also deliver the Moabites into their ___.

cards.text: Then Elisha gives the battle orders: attack every fortified city and every city of importance, cut down every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.

cards.question: The ditches are dug. When does the water show up?

answers.text: The next morning at the morning sacrifice
At sunset that very same evening
After three long days of waiting

cards.text: Water suddenly flows from the direction of Edom and fills the land, with no wind and no rain. I take back my “DIGGING?”
Meanwhile, Moab has heard the kings are coming, so everyone who can bear arms, young and old, is stationed at the border. They get up early in the morning, and the sun is shining on the water.

cards.question: From across the way, what does that water look like to the Moabites?
Red water across the way. True or false: the Moabites decide the kings have clashed swords and slaughtered one another.

cards.text: Then they shout, “Now to the plunder, Moab!” That's “this is blood” to “let's go shopping” in ONE breath.

cards.question: True or false: when the Moabites get to the camp of Israel, they find it empty.

cards.text: The Israelites rise up and attack, and the Moabites flee before them. So Israel invades their land and strikes down the Moabites.

cards.question: Israel destroys the cities and covers every good field with stones, just as Elisha said. They stop up every ___ and cut down every good ___.

cards.text: Only Kir-haraseth is left with its stones in place, but men with slings surround it and attack it as well.

cards.question: The battle is too fierce for the king of Moab. He takes seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of ___.

cards.text: They can't break through. So the king of Moab takes his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offers him as a burnt offering on the city wall.

cards.question: And there was great fury against the Israelites. What do the Israelites do?

answers.text: Withdraw and return to their own land
March on to fight the king of Edom
